market_context: United States; plain potatoes cooked without added oil or sauces
title: Boiled vs. baked potato: nutrition differences

seo.title: Boiled vs. baked potato: nutrition differences
seo.meta_description: Without added oil, boiling and baking change less than you might think. Per 100 g, baked potato is slightly more concentrated because it loses more water; eating the skin can make a larger difference to fiber.
seo.search_intent: Compare boiled and baked potato nutrition with like-for-like values and explain the effects of water, skin and toppings.

excerpt: Plain boiled and baked potatoes are nutritionally similar. USDA references for flesh without added fat put boiled potato around 87 calories per 100 g and baked flesh around 93 calories. Baking loses slightly more water and concentrates nutrients; skin and toppings usually matter more than the cooking method itself.
content_html:
A boiled potato and a baked potato feel like very different foods, but without oil, butter or toppings their basic nutrition is close. The main change is how much water remains in the potato and whether you eat the skin.

Compare plain potato flesh with plain potato flesh

A USDA reference for potato boiled in its skin and eaten as flesh provides about 87 calories, 20.1 g carbohydrate and 1.9 g protein per 100 g. Baked potato flesh without skin provides about 93 calories, 21.6 g carbohydrate and 2.0 g protein.

Per 100 gBoiled fleshBaked flesh
Calories87 kcal93 kcal
Carbohydrate20.1 g21.6 g
Protein1.9 g2.0 g
Fiber1.8 g1.5 g
Potassium379 mg391 mg

A six-calorie gap per 100 g is small. Baking has not created carbohydrate; slightly greater water loss makes the finished potato a little more concentrated.

The skin can matter more than boiling versus baking

A USDA reference for baked potato eaten with its skin provides around 93 calories, 2.2 g fiber and 535 mg potassium per 100 g. That shows why comparing a peeled boiled potato with a skin-on baked potato mixes two questions: cooking method and edible portion.

Does boiling wash nutrients away?

Some water-soluble nutrients can move into cooking water, especially when potatoes are peeled and cut into small pieces. Baking avoids direct contact with water but exposes the potato to longer dry heat. No cooking method preserves every nutrient perfectly.

Toppings create the big calorie swing

A plain 200 g baked potato is roughly 186 calories. One tablespoon of oil, about 15 g, adds roughly 135 calories. That single addition changes the dish far more than the 6-calorie-per-100-g difference between the plain cooking methods.

Which one should you choose?

Choose based on texture, recipe and what you need to add to enjoy it. When the comparison is plain potato against plain potato, boiling and baking are much closer nutritionally than their appearance suggests.

faq.question: Which has more calories, boiled or baked potato?
faq.answer: Without added fat, USDA references put boiled flesh at about 87 calories per 100 g and baked flesh at about 93 calories.

faq.question: Is baked potato healthier than boiled potato?
faq.answer: Neither is automatically healthier. Skin, toppings, portion size and the rest of the meal usually matter more.

faq.question: Does potato skin add fiber?
faq.answer: Yes. A USDA reference for baked flesh and skin contains about 2.2 g fiber per 100 g, compared with 1.5 g in baked flesh alone.
